title: House leaders: VP Sara's survey scores not a pass for unexplained wealth
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte's high ratings in opinion surveys do not give her a pass on the alleged unexplained wealth for which she has been impeached, House leaders said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 7:50pm
Vice President Sara Duterte's high ratings in opinion surveys do not give her a pass on the alleged unexplained wealth for which she has been impeached, House leaders said Wednesday.

“The point here is accountability. The impeachment trial is not based on fame, popularity in social media, or ranking in surveys. The impeachment trial is based on documents presented to support or dispute the allegations,” House Deputy Speaker Janet Garin of Iloilo said in a press conference.

“These allegations need to be addressed. No survey can erase the accountability of any high-ranking official, at naniniwala kami base sa historical data at experience natin [and we believe that based on historical data and our own experience], the Senator-judges will decide based on the documents presented, not popularity,” she added.

The answer was in response to a question about polls showing the Vice President as the frontrunner in the 2028 presidential election—an election that no one else has yet announced their intention to run for, and which she may not be eligible for if the impeachment court convicts her.

At the impeachment trial, an expert witness for the prosecution testified that Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, accumulated unexplained wealth of at least P817 million to as much as P1.5 billion.
House Deputy Speaker Jefferson Khonghun of Zambales Khonghun agreed that the impeachment process is not a popularity contest.
“The impeachment process requires transparency, accountability, especially about her wealth,” he said.
“Hindi naman tayo kinakabahan dahil hindi issue dito kung ikaw sikat o popular. Ang issue dito, ipaliwanag mo ‘yung yaman [mo]. Saan galing ang pera,” headded.
(We're not worried [about the trial outcome] because the issue here is not whether you are famous or popular. The issue is the [unexplained] wealth. Where did the money come from?)

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero earlier pointed out that even if the declared assets of the Vice President and her husband in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) from 2022 to 2025 are added up—meaning they did not spend in that period—their total declared net worth of P336 million would still be way lower than the P424 million in bank transactions recorded under the bank accounts of the Duterte-Carpio couple from 2022 to 2025 based on the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records.

Moreover, Escudero said that the that the total net worth of the Duterte-Carpio couple at P840 million as declared in their joint SALN from 2007 to 2025 is also by a mile lower than the P4.4 billion worth of bank transactions recorded under the spouses’ bank accounts from 2007 to 2025, also based from AMLC records.
The defense is yet to present a witness that disputes the P4.4 billion of bank transactions recorded under the bank accounts of the Duterte-Carpio couple.
The defense already presented at least nine witnesses so far but nobody of them disputed that P4.4 billion of bank transactions were recorded under the accounts of the Duterte-Carpio couple.
But in a television interview aired on Monday, the Vice President maintained that she is not in the wrong, considering that she has the majority of the people’s support.
Khonghun, however, responded that earning sympathy does not dispute allegations.
“She has the right to seek sympathy of the people, but again, such cannot erase the documents that has been presented by the prosecution,” he said.

“History will judge a public official on how they responded to the allegations. Kung malinis ang ating konsiyensiya, harapin at sagutin niya ang mga katanungan. Ganun lang ka simple ‘yun,” Khonghun added.
(If her conscience is clear, she should be able to face the questions and answer them. It's that simple.) — BM, GMA News
